- f'(-5) = 3(25) + 8(-5) - 3 = 75 - 40 - 3 = 32
- x1 = x0 - f(x0)/f'(x0) = -5 - (-2)/32 = -4.9375

- f'(x1) will be around 30 (no need to compute exactly for this threshold check).
- f(x1) by rough magnitude inspection of terms looks very small, on the order of 10^-3.
- Then update size |x2 - x1| ≈ |f(x1)/f'(x1)| ≈ 10^-3 / 30 ≈ 3×10^-5, which is below the 4-decimal rounding threshold (5×10^-5).
Given that, x1 and x2 should round to the same 4-decimal value without needing a full precise recomputation. So the smallest n at which x_n and x_{n+1} match after rounding is n = 1.
